title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the 2020 Committee report on AI and Public Standards outlines steps to improve how artificial intelligence is developed, tested, and used across public services. It calls for stronger regulatory frameworks, increased investment in AI research, and greater public engagement to ensure AI systems are transparent, fair, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep assessments fair, secure and transparent. The policy describes guidelines, monitoring steps and cooperation with schools, exam bodies and other stakeholders to manage AI’s role in exam design, delivery and grading.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report evaluates how copyrighted works are used in training and developing AI systems, highlighting both the potential benefits and the legal challenges involved. It offers recommendations and policy guidelines to help creators, developers, and regulators balance innovation with respect for copyright rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government confirms it will take the Lords Select Committee’s recommendations seriously, pledging to strengthen AI regulation, boost research and development, and protect consumers and workers. It stresses that the UK will lead in safe, responsible AI while fostering innovation and international cooperation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document lays out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes a FAQ section to explain the committee’s role, processes, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines recommendations and perspectives on how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping the regulatory framework for medical products, focusing on integrating AI-driven tools into safety, efficacy, and approval processes. It adopts the AI White Paper principles—such as transparency, accountability, and continuous oversight—to ensure that AI technologies used in medical products meet rigorous standards for patient safety and ethical deployment.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a plan to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI-driven defence body in the world, given its size. It focuses on advancing AI capabilities to strengthen national defence while upholding high standards of reliability and trust.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This plan details how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to leverage AI benefits while mitigating risks. It outlines strategies, partnerships, and safeguards to ensure responsible AI adoption.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright works are used to train and develop AI systems, assessing compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s Section 137. It highlights progress made, identifies challenges, and recommends best practices for balancing innovation with copyright protection.
